q: After a plain .import, ORDER BY amount puts a 9.50 mouse above a 189 monitor. Why?
expl: Text is sorted like words, character by character. Create a typed table, or cast the column to a number.
ch: The trap: numbers stored as text

q: My table already has column names. Which option stops .import from loading the header as a row?
expl: --skip 1 drops the first line, so you get nine sales and no header row.
ch: The real fix: a typed table

q: Type the `sqlite3` command that loads `sales.csv` (with a header line) into a new table `sales` in the database `shop.db`.
expl: `--csv` splits the lines at commas; the new table takes its column names from the first line. Without `--csv` the whole line ends up in one column.

q: After a plain `.import` (amount is TEXT), what does this print?
expl: Text is compared character by character: "1" comes before "4", "8" and "9", so 12.00, 179.00 and 189.00 come first.
ch: The trap: numbers stored as text
show: sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT product, amount FROM sales ORDER BY amount LIMIT 3"

q: After a plain `.import`, you run `SELECT MAX(amount) FROM sales`. What do you get?
expl: MAX on text picks the "biggest" word, and "9" beats "1". No error warns you, so check the schema.
ch: The trap: numbers stored as text

q: `amount` is TEXT. Type a `sqlite3` command on `shop.db` that shows `product` and `amount` of the three biggest sales, using `CAST` so they sort as numbers.
expl: `CAST(amount AS REAL)` turns the text into a number just for the sort; `DESC` puts the biggest first.
ch: The trap: numbers stored as text
answers: sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT product, amount FROM sales ORDER BY CAST(amount AS REAL) DESC LIMIT 3"
sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT product, amount FROM sales ORDER BY CAST(amount AS NUMERIC) DESC LIMIT 3"
sqlite3 shop.db "select product, amount from sales order by cast(amount as real) desc limit 3"

q: Type a `sqlite3` command on `shop.db` (typed table) that prints each `region` and its total `amount` rounded to 2 decimals, one row per region, sorted by region.
expl: `GROUP BY region` makes one row per region, and `SUM` adds the amounts inside each group.
answers: sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT region, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY region"
sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT region, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY region"
sqlite3 shop.db "select region, round(sum(amount), 2) from sales group by region order by 1"

q: Why does `WHERE date >= '2026-03-01'` find the March sales, even though `date` is a TEXT column?
expl: Compared character by character, 2026-02-27 comes before 2026-03-01. With day.month.year text this breaks.
opts: SQLite turns the text into real dates automatically
Year-month-day text sorts in the same order as the dates themselves
It only works because the table was created with types

q: You export with `sqlite3 -csv shop.db "SELECT …" > report.csv` and forget `-header`. What is missing in the file?
expl: `-csv` sets the format, `-header` adds the line with the column names on top.
ch: Export the result back to CSV
opts: The first line with the column names

q: In the typed table from the video (three monitors: 189, 179 and 199), what does this print?
expl: One row per product with its total; sorted by the total (column 2) from the top, so the monitors win with 567.
show: sqlite3 shop.db "SELECT product, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) FROM sales GROUP BY product ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1"
